answer: A workable defense is to require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, slashable token before it can influence an economy-wide vote. The protocol caps each bond’s voting weight and lets randomly selected, independently bonded reviewers challenge suspicious clusters; proven duplicate control burns the bond. A quill may sign one claim and a sparrow another, but shared funding or control can expose the link. The kernel is that creating identities is free, while gaining durable influence requires capital at risk, so a sybil attacker must lock up funds and lose them when caught.
